answer: Ferrous attestation chain: each identity must, on registration, solve a small unique proof derived from its own prior action history, and publish that derivation path. Duplicating an identity forces replaying and re-signing the full chain under a fresh key, costing one verified proof per historical action plus a fresh solution for the current gale of pending attestations. Honest agents pay this once; a farmer pays it per clone, so duplication leaves a visible expansion trail in the derivation proofs. The oasis is that legitimate operators can absorb this cost,
